NEET UG Merit List 2026: Your Comprehensive Guide to Results, Cut-offs, and Counselling

The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET UG) is the gateway to undergraduate medical and dental courses in India. For aspirants of NEET UG 2026, the period following the examination is filled with anticipation for the NEET UG Merit List 2026, results, and the subsequent counselling process. This year, the journey has seen significant developments, including a re-examination, making it crucial for candidates to stay informed about every detail.

The initial NEET UG 2026 examination, held on May 3, 2026, was unfortunately cancelled due to allegations of a paper leak. In response, the National Testing Agency (NTA) swiftly conducted a re-examination on June 21, 2026, across numerous centres in India and abroad. Now, all eyes are on the release of the NEET UG 2026 results and the much-awaited merit lists, which will pave the way for admissions into MBBS, BDS, and other allied medical courses.

Understanding the NEET UG 2026 Merit List

The NEET UG Merit List is not a singular entity but rather a compilation of various lists that determine eligibility for different quotas and institutions. The National Testing Agency (NTA) is responsible for releasing the primary merit lists based on the candidates' performance.

✅ All India Rank (AIR) List: This comprehensive list, released by the NTA, includes the overall ranks of all qualified candidates who appeared for NEET UG 2026.

✅ 15% All India Quota (AIQ) Merit List: This list is crucial for admission to 15% of the total MBBS/BDS seats across government medical colleges in India, as well as seats in central universities, deemed universities, AIIMS, and JIPMER. The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) uses this list for its counselling rounds.

✅ 85% State Quota Merit Lists: Individual state counselling authorities prepare and release their own merit lists for the remaining 85% of seats in government medical colleges and other state-level institutions, based on domicile and eligibility criteria.

Key Dates and Official Websites

While the exact dates are still being finalized, here's what candidates can expect:

The NEET UG 2026 results, including those from the re-examination, are anticipated to be declared in the second week of July, possibly around July 15, 2026. Candidates can check their scorecards, percentile details, and All India Rank on the official NTA website: neet.nta.nic.in.

Following the result declaration, the NEET UG counselling process is expected to commence in the first week of July and may continue until September 2026. The official MCC website, mcc.nic.in, will be the primary portal for All India Quota counselling.

NEET UG 2026 Cut-off: What to Expect

Understanding the NEET UG cut-off is paramount. There are two main types:

  • Qualifying Cut-off: This is the minimum percentile/score required to be eligible for the counselling process.
  • Admission Cut-off: This is the much higher score needed to actually secure a seat in a particular medical or dental college.

Based on current trends and the re-examination, here's an overview of the expected qualifying cut-off marks:

Category Expected Qualifying Marks (Re-NEET 2026) Expected Percentile
General Category (UR) 130-150 marks (out of 720) 50th percentile
SC/ST/OBC 113-143 marks (approx.) 40th percentile
General-PwD (UR-PwD) 127-143 marks (approx.) 45th percentile
OBC-PH/SC-PH/ST-PH 113-126 marks (approx.) 40th percentile

For securing a government MBBS seat, a score of 610+ is generally considered safe. For top AIQ colleges, candidates should aim for scores above 650, with premier institutions like AIIMS Delhi often requiring 680-700+ marks.

The NEET UG 2026 Counselling Process: Your Step-by-Step Guide

The counselling process is a multi-stage procedure conducted online for the most part. It typically involves four main rounds: Round 1, Round 2, Mop-Up Round, and Stray Vacancy Round.

1. Check Result and Rank
After the results are declared, thoroughly check your NEET score, All India Rank, category rank, and qualifying status.
2. Online Registration
For All India Quota (AIQ) seats, register on the official Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) portal (mcc.nic.in). For state quota seats, register on the respective state counselling authority websites. This usually involves entering your NEET roll number, personal details, creating a password, and paying the registration and security fees.
3. Choice Filling and Locking
Select your preferred colleges and courses based on your rank, category, and seat matrix. You can choose multiple options and arrange them in order of preference. Ensure you lock your choices before the deadline.
4. Seat Allotment Result
The MCC and state authorities will release the seat allotment results based on merit, preferences, category, and seat availability.
5. Download Allotment Letter and Report to College
If you are allotted a seat, download the provisional allotment letter and report to the assigned college within the stipulated timeframe for document verification and admission confirmation. This is typically the only offline part of the process.
6. Participate in Subsequent Rounds (if needed)
If you are not satisfied with your allotted seat or were not allotted one in the initial rounds, you can participate in subsequent rounds like Round 2, Mop-Up Round, and Stray Vacancy Round.

Essential Documents for NEET UG 2026 Counselling

Preparation is key. Ensure you have the following documents ready, both originals and photocopies, before counselling begins:

✅ NEET UG 2026 Scorecard

✅ NEET UG 2026 Admit Card

✅ Class 10th Marksheet and Certificate (for Date of Birth proof)

✅ Class 12th Marksheet and Passing Certificate

✅ Valid Photo ID Proof (Aadhaar Card, Passport, etc.)

✅ Passport-size Photographs (same as used in NEET application)

✅ Provisional Seat Allotment Letter (downloaded from MCC portal)

✅ Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS, if applicable)

✅ PwD Certificate (if applicable)

✅ Domicile Certificate (for state quota counselling)

✅ Migration Certificate

✅ Fee Payment Receipt

✅ Character Certificate

✅ Transfer Certificate

✅ Medical Fitness Certificate

Navigating Tie-Breaking Criteria

In instances where two or more candidates secure the same marks, a specific set of tie-breaking rules is applied to determine their ranks:

1. Higher Marks in Biology
Candidates with higher marks in Biology (Botany and Zoology) will be given preference.
2. Higher Marks in Chemistry
If the tie persists, the candidate with higher marks in Chemistry will be ranked higher.
3. Higher Marks in Physics
If the tie still remains, candidates with higher marks in Physics will be considered.
4. Fewer Incorrect Answers
Finally, if marks remain equal across all subjects, candidates with fewer incorrect answers across all subjects will be ranked higher.

The NEET UG 2026 journey has been a challenging one for many, but with the re-examination concluded, clarity on results and counselling is on the horizon. Staying informed, preparing your documents, and understanding the process will be critical in securing your dream medical seat. We wish all the aspirants the very best!
